title: Relative first cohomology and torsors with a specified open section
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion, and $j:V=T\setminus Z\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement. Let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Use the derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. A $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor] means a sheaf of sets with a $G$-action which is locally equivariantly isomorphic to $G$ acting on itself. Use derived global sections $R\Gamma$ and their cohomology as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and the mapping cone and shift of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put
$$H^q(T,V;G)=H^q\bigl(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,G)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(V,j^{-1}G))[-1]\bigr).$$
There is a canonical bijection between $H^1(T,V;G)$ and the isomorphism classes of pairs $(P,s)$ consisting of a $G$-torsor $P$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and a section $s\in(j^{-1}P)(V)$; isomorphisms must carry the specified section to the specified section. It sends the trivial torsor with its identity section to zero. The map $H^1(T,V;G)\to H^1(T,G)$ forgets $s$ and gives the ordinary torsor class. This bijection is natural under morphisms $G\to G'$ (contracted product of torsors [def-sc-contracted-product-presentation]) and under morphisms of schemes $h:T'\to T$, with $V'=h^{-1}V$, followed by any coefficient morphism $h^{-1}G\to G'$.
For any short exact sequence $0\to G_1\to G_2\to G_3\to0$, the relative groups have the natural connecting maps $H^q(T,V;G_3)\to H^{q+1}(T,V;G_1)$; these commute with forgetting the specified support and with the preceding pullback and coefficient maps.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1 (ordinary torsor class via its canonical extension); relative extension of this construction as needed in the item. Compare cohomology.tex Tag 0G71, lemma-triangle-sections-with-support, and Tag 0G78, remark-support-functorial. The relative refinement and its functoriality are agent-stated, not claimed verbatim in 03AJ.

proof.text: Choose a resolution $0\to G\xrightarrow{\epsilon}I^0\xrightarrow d I^1\to\cdots$ with zero negative terms. Enough injectives and the bounded-below injective representative theorem supply it and say it is K-injective. The open restriction $j^{-1}I$ is K-injective: restriction is right adjoint to the exact extension-by-zero functor, so the right-adjoint K-injectivity theorem applies, with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. Exact inverse image makes it a resolution of $j^{-1}G$. Thus both terms of the relative cone are computed by $A^r=I^r(T)$ and $B^r=(j^{-1}I^r)(V)$, with restriction $r:A\to B$.

Use the signed model $C^n=A^n\oplus B^{n-1}$ with $D(a,b)=(da,r(a)-db)$ for $\operatorname{Cone}(r)[-1]$. This is the cone convention in the cited definition, after changing the sign on the $B$ summand; $D^2=0$ since $rd=dr$. In degree one its cocycles are pairs $a\in I^1(T)$, $b\in(j^{-1}I^0)(V)$ with $da=0$ and $r(a)=db$. Its boundaries are $(dx,r(x))$ for $x\in I^0(T)$, since $B^{-1}=0$.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: For a cocycle $(a,b)$ form the sheaf $P_a$ of solutions $t\in I^0$ to $dt=a$ (on each etale object use the restriction of $a$). Exactness of the resolution says $I^0\to\ker(d:I^1\to I^2)$ is epi; local surjectivity therefore supplies such solutions on a covering. Two solutions differ by a unique section of $G=\ker(d:I^0\to I^1)$, so addition through $\epsilon$ makes $P_a$ a $G$-torsor. The equation $db=r(a)$ makes $b$ a specified section on $V$. If $(a',b')=(a,b)+(dx,r(x))$, translation $t\mapsto t+x$ is a torsor isomorphism carrying $b$ to $b'$. This constructs a map from $H^1(C)$ to pairs modulo section-preserving isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: This map is injective. Given a section-preserving equivariant isomorphism $F:P_a\to P_{a'}$, on any object admitting a section $t$ put $x=F(t)-t\in I^0$. For another section $t+\epsilon(g)$ equivariance gives $F(t+\epsilon(g))-(t+\epsilon(g))=F(t)-t$. These local sections therefore agree on overlaps and glue, by the sheaf axiom for $I^0$, to $x\in I^0(T)$. Applying $d$ gives $dx=a'-a$, and evaluating on the specified open section gives $r(x)=b'-b$. The two cocycles differ by the boundary $D(x)$ computed in step 2.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: For surjectivity take a pair $(P,s)$. The named canonical extension in the statement of the absolute torsor theorem gives $0\to G\to E_P\xrightarrow p\mathbf Z_T\to0$, whose fibre over $1$ is $P$. By injectivity of $I^0$, extend $\epsilon:G\to I^0$ across $G\hookrightarrow E_P$ to $f:E_P\to I^0$. The composite $df$ kills $G$, hence factors through $p$ as $\bar a:\mathbf Z_T\to I^1$; let $a=\bar a(1)$. Since $d\bar a=0$, $da=0$. Set $b=f(s)$ on $V$, so $db=r(a)$. On the fibre over $1$, $f$ is equivariant and takes values in $P_a$; locally choosing a point of $P$ identifies this map with a translation $G\to G$, hence it is an isomorphism and carries $s$ to $b$. Different extensions $f'$ differ by a morphism $\mathbf Z_T\to I^0$, hence by a global $x$, giving exactly $(a',b')-(a,b)=(dx,r(x))$. We have proved a bijection, rather than selected an arbitrary lift of the ordinary torsor class.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: For $(a,b)=(0,0)$, $P_a=\epsilon(G)$ and its open section is zero, the identity section of the additive torsor. Projection $C\to A$ sends $(a,b)$ to $a$. In the extension of step 5, $f$ lifts the section $1$ to degree zero of the resolution, and its differential is $a$. Thus the connecting class $\delta_{E_P}(1)$ is $[a]$. The absolute torsor theorem names exactly this class as the ordinary class of $P$. Consequently projection is the required forgetful map, with the asserted normalization.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: The construction is independent of resolutions and natural in coefficients and schemes. For $h:T'\to T$ and $\varphi:h^{-1}G\to G'$, choose a nonnegative injective resolution $J$ of $G'$. Exactness makes $h^{-1}I$ a resolution of $h^{-1}G$. Extend the augmentation map into $J^0$ by injectivity; inductively the already defined differential factors through the next image in $h^{-1}I$, and extend this map into the next injective term of $J$. This constructs a chain map $u:h^{-1}I\to J$ lifting $\varphi$. Its unique homotopy class is the one supplied by K-injective Hom-to-derived bijectivity; here the source need not be injective. Sections and their restrictions give $U_A:A\to A'$, $U_B:B\to B'$ with $U_Br=r'U_A$. The resulting map on $C$ sends $(a,b)$ to $(U_Aa,U_Bb)$. If two comparisons differ by $dH+Hd$, the homotopy on these signed cones is $(a,b)\mapsto(Ha,-Hb)$; substituting $D$ gives $DH_C+H_CD$. Hence comparison choices give the same cohomology map; identity comparisons and composite comparisons prove independence and composition. By the cited cohomology pullback definition this is the derived pullback and coefficient map on the relative cone.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: Inverse image commutes with finite limits of underlying sheaves of sets and with their abelian structures, so preserves the kernel-and-fibre construction of $P_a$. The absolute etale torsor functoriality theorem guarantees that $h^{-1}P_a$ remains a torsor. The contracted-product existence theorem supplies its sheaf quotient. The chain map $u$ of step 7 therefore gives an equivariant morphism $h^{-1}P_a\to P_{U_Aa}$ under $\varphi$; it sends the pulled-back chosen section to $U_Bb$. It induces an isomorphism from the contracted product $h^{-1}P_a\wedge^{h^{-1}G}G'$: locally pick a section $t$ of the source torsor, and both torsors become $G'$; the map is $g'\mapsto u(t)+g'$, a translation. These local identifications agree by equivariance and the defining quotient relation of the contracted product. For the coefficient identity this is just inverse image of the torsor. Thus the bijection, including its specified section, is natural for every $\varphi$, without assuming $h^{-1}G=G'$.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1; relative injective-resolution refinement written here

proof.text: For a short exact coefficient sequence choose a horseshoe of nonnegative injective resolutions $I_1,I_2,I_3$. Its degreewise short exact rows split since the first term is injective. Taking sections on $T$ or $V$, and then the finite sums defining $C(I_k)$, preserves those split rows. Thus $0\to C(I_1)\to C(I_2)\to C(I_3)\to0$ is degreewise short exact. The complex long-exact-sequence theorem supplies $\delta^q_{T,V}$. Explicitly lift a relative cocycle $z$ to $y\in C(I_2)^q$; $Dy$ lies in the image of $C(I_1)^{q+1}$, and the class of its unique preimage is $\delta[z]$. The projections to $A(I_k)$ form a morphism of these short exact complex sequences, so long-exact-sequence naturality proves compatibility with forgetting support.

source.place: Ordinary horseshoe construction as in Tag 03AJ; Derived Categories Tag 013T, lemma-injective-resolution-ses; relative cone calculation written here

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-signed-fibre-triangulated] with $A=\Gamma(T,-)$, $B=\Gamma(V,j^{-1}(-))$ and $r$ restriction. These are additive functors by the sectionwise abelian group operations. It supplies the exact homotopy functor $F_T$, the shift comparison $(a,b)\mapsto(a,-b)$ and the cone comparison $(x,y,z,w)\mapsto(x,z,y,-w)$, with the boundary $-p$ respected. By step 1 and the definition of derived sections, its value on an injective representative computes exactly the relative cone in the statement, not a different cohomology theory.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; relative cone proof of functoriality, compare Cohomology Tags 0G71 and 0G78

proof.text: Apply [lem-amb-bounded-injective-fibre-descent] to this $F_T$, first with $E=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tau=\mathrm{id}$. Enough injectives holds for the etale abelian-sheaf category by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. We obtain an exact functor $RF_T$ on $D^+$, computed on the same bounded below injective complexes as in steps 1 and 9, and canonical identifications under changes of those representatives. Thus it is legitimate to apply the relative construction to every derived coefficient morphism, including a boundary into a shift.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; relative cone proof of functoriality, compare Cohomology Tags 0G71 and 0G78

proof.text: Split the horseshoe rows of step 9, writing $I_2=I_1\oplus I_3$ with differential $\begin{pmatrix}d_1&t\\0&d_3\end{pmatrix}$. The split-connecting-morphism node gives the chain map $t:I_3\to I_1[1]$. The split-boundary comparison identifies its derived class with the canonical cone boundary. Naturality of the complex-SES triangle for the horseshoe augmentation therefore identifies this class with the coefficient boundary $w:G_3\to G_1[1]$. For the relative split sequence the off-diagonal is $(a,b)\mapsto(t_Ta,-t_Vb)$, since its second differential is $r-d_V$. This is $s_{I_1}F_T(t)$. The split connecting formula now says that the lift-and-differentiate boundary in step 9 is $H^q(s_{I_1}RF_T(w))$. This also fixes its sign.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; relative cone proof of functoriality, compare Cohomology Tags 0G71 and 0G78

proof.text: For $h:T'\to T$ and $V'=h^{-1}V$ apply [lem-amb-bounded-injective-fibre-descent] with $E=h^{-1}$, $F=F_T$, $F'=F_{T'}$. Exactness of $E$ is [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The sheaf adjunction unit gives the section maps on $T$ and $V$ and their restriction square (the same square as step 7); its naturality is part of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. These maps define $\tau$. They commute with the signed shift comparison because they act separately on the two summands. The descent lemma makes the comparison natural for all derived morphisms and shifts, including $w$. Its absolute component is precisely the pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit]. It remains to see that $D^+h^{-1}(w)$ is the boundary $w'$ of the pulled-back sequence $0\to h^{-1}G_1\to h^{-1}G_2\to h^{-1}G_3\to0$. By step 12, $w=Q(\epsilon_1)[1]^{-1}Q(t)Q(\epsilon_3)$ for the horseshoe augmentations $\epsilon_k$. Applying the additive exact functor $h^{-1}$ termwise to the split horseshoe gives a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes, with the pulled-back splitting maps, resolving the pulled-back coefficient sequence; its split boundary $\pi d s$ is $h^{-1}t$ [lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-connecting-morphism]. By [lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison] its canonical boundary is $Q(h^{-1}t)$, and naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] for the quasi-isomorphic augmentation $h^{-1}\epsilon$ gives $w'=Q(h^{-1}\epsilon_1)[1]^{-1}Q(h^{-1}t)Q(h^{-1}\epsilon_3)$. Since the derived inverse image is computed termwise compatibly with shifts [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], this is $D^+h^{-1}(w)$. Applying $H^q$ to the naturality square for $w$ and substituting step 12 on $T$ and on $T'$ proves pullback compatibility of the relative connecting maps.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open; relative cone proof of functoriality, compare Cohomology Tags 0G71 and 0G78

proof.text: For a morphism of coefficient short exact sequences, use [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift] within the same sheaf category to lift it to the two chosen horseshoes. Taking sections and relative cones gives a morphism of the split short exact complex sequences of step 9. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] its connecting square commutes. Apply this also to the identity coefficient-sequence morphism and two choices of horseshoe; the representative identifications from step 11 identify the horizontal comparisons with the identity derived maps. Thus the boundaries are independent of horseshoe choices. Combine coefficient naturality with step 13 for pullback followed by any coefficient map, and with step 9's projection square for forgetting support. These are all the claimed connecting-map compatibilities.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NQ-da3ebf99c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: FIX for one citation gap (C4) in step 13; everything else passes. I read the item in full (14 steps), both new nodes, and the statement of every cited node. I checked the sources: Stacks derived.tex 014E definition-cone and 05TK lemma-resolution-functor-quasi-inverse (with its proof), the tags 013T, 0152, 05TN, 03AJ and 08FI in tags/tags, and the blueprint text of the ancestor lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map in main-20261015. The statement, Lean record and steps 1-9 are equal to the returned side-DAG node. This is not a target node, so the base-change morphism and coefficient-category checks do not apply here; the coefficients are Ab(T_et), unchanged, and no SGA source is cited. I recomputed every sign of lem-amb-signed-fibre-triangulated: the cone isomorphism Phi=(x,z,y,-w), the boundary (both routes give (-y,w)), the shift (a,b)->(a,-b) and the homotopy (Ha,-Hb). I tested it with r=id, r=0, A=0 and complexes in one degree. lem-amb-bounded-injective-fibre-descent is true: 05TK gives the equivalence, and J is K-injective so the comparison map u exists and is unique up to homotopy. E need not preserve injectives. In step 12 I checked t=pi d s and that the off-diagonal (t_T a,-t_V b) equals s F_T(t). Neither new node duplicates an existing one or restates a clause of the item. There is no cycle. The new off-unit tool uses are lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison and three Mathlib leaves; I accept them. Fault (C4): step 13 used the formula delta=-p q^{-1} for the boundary of a short exact sequence, which no cited statement gives; lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle only says a natural delta exists. The result is true and follows from nodes the item already cites. I rewrote step 13 to derive D^+h^{-1}(w)=w' through the pulled-back split horseshoe, using lem-weil-pbc-degreewise-split-connecting-morphism, lem-sc-p1-split-ses-boundary-comparison, triangle naturality and def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image. That definition is added to proof_deps and declared in split_report.tool_uses. The corrected item is fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology.json, and the full checks are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
